## Lesson Objectives {data-background-image="/images/37/37.webp" data-background-opacity="0.1"}

- Describe why AI is __difficult to safeguard__
- Define __algorithmic bias__ and articulate why it is dangerous
- Define the term __deepfake__ and discuss some strategies for spotting them
- Evaluate the __ethical__ and __social__ implications of AI in military and civilian applications.

## Limitations of Artificial Intelligence

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=60%}
- Model Opacity
    - Difficult to understand decisions
    - How to explain the output of neural networks?
- Data Bias
    - Results are only as good as the data
    - Decisions can have unintended consequences
- Hallucination
    - AI can generate realistic-looking wrong goutput
    - What could possibly go wrong?
- **How do you safeguard AI?**
:::
::: {.column width=40%}
![](https://imgs.xkcd.com/comics/machine_learning.png){width="100%"}
:::
::::


## Algorithmic Bias

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Language models trained on massive datasets
    - Where do the datasets come from?
    - What biases could be present?
- Who holds the power to decide what is "fair"?
- What are the consequences of biased AI?

## [DoD Ethical Framework for AI](https://www.defense.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/2091996/) {.smaller}

1. **Responsible**. DoD personnel will exercise appropriate levels of judgment and care, while remaining responsible for the development, deployment, and use of AI capabilities.
1. **Equitable**. The Department will take deliberate steps to minimize unintended bias in AI capabilities.
1. **Traceable**. The Department’s AI capabilities will be developed and deployed such that relevant personnel possess an appropriate understanding of the technology, development processes, and operational methods applicable to AI capabilities, including with transparent and auditable methodologies, data sources, and design procedure and documentation.
1. **Reliable**. The Department’s AI capabilities will have explicit, well-defined uses, and the safety, security, and effectiveness of such capabilities will be subject to testing and assurance within those defined uses across their entire life-cycles.
1. **Governable**. The Department will design and engineer AI capabilities to fulfill their intended functions while possessing the ability to detect and avoid unintended consequences, and the ability to disengage or deactivate deployed systems that demonstrate unintended behavior.
